title: 720,000 Russian soldiers killed since start of Ukraine war, new data suggests | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

Almost three-quarters of a million Russian soldiers have been killed since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, equating to roughly one deathevery four minutes, analysis based on leaked official data has revealed.

Russian opposition outletsMediazonaandMeduzareported on Monday that by the end of September, 490,000 Russian troops had been confirmed dead by Russia’s statistical bureau, Rosstat.

But accounting for time lags in reporting and including troops who have been reported as missing in action – and are most likely dead – Russian fatalities jump to more than 720,000 since the start of the war, according to the two outlets.

That is a staggering number that surpasses Russia’s death toll from the Soviet war in Afghanistan in the 1980s and both Chechen wars in the 1990s and early 2000s – and which the Kremlin has long tried to keep secret.

Rosstat stopped publishing demographic data in 2025 to disguise the rising death toll from the war. Mediazona and Meduza, as well as other outlets, obtained the official data after two pro-Ukrainian hacker groups, Cyber ​​Partisans of Belarus and Silent Crow, managed to breach Rosstat’s servers earlier this month.

CNN cannot independently verify the figures, but the leaked data on confirmed deaths alonecorroborates earlier estimatesby analysts and Western intelligence – which now appear to fall far short of the likely real death toll.

Mediazona and Meduza have long been keeping a tally of Russian losses, based mostly on inheritance documents, death notices and other publicly available documents.

But the leaked Rosstat data allowed the media outlets to go a step further, using the same methods and calculations normally employed by actuaries estimating risks and insurance premiums.

By analyzing discrepancies between reported death dates and death registration dates, and by comparing these to search notices published by relatives, the reporters were able to extrapolate the number of deaths that have occurred but have not yet been reported to be somewhere around 230,000.

Mediazona has kept a tally of troops identified as missing by their relatives from 2023. That database contains 160,000 individuals and almost all of them are likely dead. Mediazona said that based on its reporting, the rate of survival among those reported missing only around 10%.

The data shared by Silent Crow showed that the war was the fourth most common cause of death in Russia since the start of the full-scale invasion, after heart diseases; Covid; and stroke and other vascular conditions.It also confirms what has long been suspected – that the losses are not spread evenly across Russia, with poorer areas and ethnic minorities suffering significantly higher casualty rates.

In addition, an analysis by the NEST Centre, a think tank that also obtained the data, revealed the scale of Russia’s recruitment of foreign fighters. It identified 6,947 records of foreign nationals killed in Ukraine – the majority of them from the central Asian countries of Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan, and Turkmenistan.

Like Russia, Ukraine doesn’t release official casualty data, although Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has publicly acknowledged the scale of losses in combat. The most recent research by the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) estimated in July that the country has endured between 525,000 and 625,000 casualties, including 125,000 and 150,000 fatalities.

Alexander Baunov, a senior fellow at the Carnegie Russia Eurasia Center, said that the combined death toll suffered by Russia and Ukraine could exceed 1 million.

As the newly projected death toll underscores the human cost of Moscow’s war, fears are growing in Ukraine over a deteriorating security situation in the country’s eastern Donetsk region – an area mostly under Russian control – amid dailyguided bomb and drone attacks.

All families with children still in Donetsk were on Tuesday ordered to evacuate.

Children and families in many communities in most of Ukrainian-controlled Donetsk - including the major cities of Kramatorsk and Sloviansk - were already under the evacuation order, but now the measure has been expanded to settlements further west. An estimated 64,500 civilians remain in the region as of November 2026, according to the Donetsk regional military administration.

“This is an extremely difficult but necessary decision. The Russians are shelling our cities and villages every day and bombarding the region with aerial bombs,” said the head of Donetsk’s regional military administration, Vadym Filashkin.

For months, Moscow’s forces have been inching towardsKramatorsk, one of Ukraine’s last strongholds in the north of Donetsk region. Tuesday’s mandatory evacuation order is a sign of Kyiv’s concern that an expansion of Russian attacks could further harm civilians and isolate communities, for example by blowing up bridges and supply routes.

CNN’s Clare Sebastian, Nathan Hodge, Kosta Gak and Lauren Kent contributed reporting.

CNN’s Clare Sebastian, Nathan Hodge, Kosta Gak and Lauren Kent contributed reporting.
